text: If the Sun vanished right now, you wouldn't even notice for eight minutes and twenty seconds.
That's how long sunlight takes to reach us. And gravity travels at exactly the same speed.
So for eight minutes, Earth keeps happily circling a Sun that isn't there.
Then, lights out. Even the Moon goes dark. It was only ever a mirror.
With nothing to orbit, Earth flies off in a straight line, at thirty kilometers every second.
The Moon tags along for the ride, still orbiting us, in the dark.
Luckily, you won't freeze instantly. Unluckily, the first days each get about twenty degrees colder.
Within a week, the whole planet is below freezing.
The oceans freeze on top, but that ice works like a blanket. Underneath, the water stays liquid for thousands of years.
And down by the volcanic vents, tube worms and shrimp that never needed sunlight just carry on.
So the real survivors of the apocalypse? The shrimp.
